Hi Anita — thanks for the summary and the MAP template.

We can definitely run a staged MAP for GCP private offer activation. Sketch below — I put estimated lead times next to each gate:

1) Formal acceptance (you confirm evaluation success) — 1 business day
2) Draft MAP & responsibilities (we'll populate your template) — 2 business days
3) PO issued by Orpheon to Redwood Billing — dependent on your internal AP (target within 5 business days)
4) Redwood legal review of PO/terms & sign — 2–3 business days if standard terms
5) Cloud vendor private offer ingestion & activation (GCP PO acceptance) — 7–10 business days after PO + signed terms
6) Production enablement & onboarding sprint — 3–5 business days after activation

Short-term asks for your team: please confirm which billing route you prefer (GCP Marketplace private offer vs. direct invoice). Marketplace private offers are typically faster to reconcile on your cloud console; direct invoices require our AP to accept your vendor onboarding (which sometimes adds time).

I'll populate the MAP (updated filename: Orpheon-MAP-v2.xlsx) and loop in Ben for billing specifics. Propose a 30-min kickoff next Tuesday 6/27 at 10am PT — does that work for you and Thomas?

Best,

Thanks Rachel / Anita — looping Grace for finance/ops. Quick notes on billing paths and minimal checklist so procurement has visibility: 

Options (pros/cons):
- GCP Marketplace Private Offer (recommended for Orpheon):
  - Pros: charges show up in your cloud billing, simplifies chargeback inside your org; private offer ingestion typically completes in 7–10 business days after we accept PO and GCP processes the offer.
  - Cons: requires Orpheon to have appropriate Cloud Billing permissions to see commits if you want account-level visibility.
- Direct monthly invoicing from Redwood:
  - Pros: simple legal flow for some customers; invoice goes directly to AP.
  - Cons: vendor onboarding can add 5–10 business days; requires net-terms setup and a PO referencing the Redwood contract id.

Minimal checklist for a fast ingestion:
- PO generated and emailed to billing@redwood.ai with line items referencing deal id RDW-ORP-2028-042
- Signed terms or confirmation of Redwood standard terms (attached: Redwood-PrivateOffer-Terms.pdf)
- Vendor onboarding form (if doing direct invoicing) — we can accept electronically

I'll prep a short billing one-pager and can join the kickoff call. Grace — can you confirm whether Redwood needs a separate reseller addendum for Orpheon on GCP private offers?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Strategic Accounts — Billing & Renewals | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachments: Redwood-PrivateOffer-Terms.pdf (PDF, 4 pages)

Looping in a short ops note so expectations are aligned:

- For GCP private offer ingestion we need: signed PO, acceptance of Redwood terms (or redlines early), and the target billing account/project id from Orpheon. Once we have those, expect ~7 business days for ingestion in typical cases.
- If Orpheon prefers AWS Marketplace path instead, ingestion timelines are similar but we need the aws-account-id and marketplace AMI/sku mapping earlier.
- On the MAP: include a gating item for security/compliance acceptance (SOC2 scope) if Orpheon will route regulated workloads. That gate often adds coordination time with our security team — plan for 5 extra business days if triggered.
